value.overview: The Boat-tailed Grackle (Quiscalus major) is a blackbird recorded in the United States. Field recognition often comes from large glossy blackbird, very long tail, heavy bill, and inflated display posture in males. In the U.S. source data, it appeared in 13 state or DC summaries, including AL, DE, FL, GA, LA, MD, MS, NC, NJ, NY, SC, TX, VA. It is most associated with Coasts:  Saltmarsh and Wetlands:  Freshwater Marsh, and local season should be checked before trip planning.
value.classification: The Boat-tailed Grackle belongs to the family Troupials and Allies in the order Passeriformes. This is the practical birding classification used for the BirdIntel profile cache.
value.identification: Look for large glossy blackbird, very long tail, heavy bill, and inflated display posture in males. Also use size, posture, flight style, voice, behavior, habitat, and season. Plumage can vary by sex, age, molt, and light, so the safest identification comes from combining several field marks rather than relying on one color or feature.
